author: WP01
summary: Reading routes through the book for twelve kinds of reader, plus a shortest route to a first program and a procedure for localising renderer-specific results. The routes are book navigation, but several carry current technical distinctions (diagnostics build versus runtime choices, renderer selection latch, binding ABI versus package parity, host classes of evidence) that the site already documents; the localisation procedure was missing and is now on the compatibility and evidence page.

concepts.text: Readers are routed by role (new user, porter, renderer implementer, runtime renderer user, native C consumer, platform implementer, Content Pipeline, Diagnostics/Inspector, binding author, framework, glTF and verification contributors) to chapters in a recommended order.
concepts.note: Book navigation; the site's own hubs (documentation.html, development/index.html, deep-dives hub) serve this role.

concepts.text: For renderer users, compiled families, the configured default, the runtime preference, fallback and the first-device latch are separate things to understand before choosing a renderer.
For Diagnostics and the Inspector, the build-time OFF/STATS/FULL level, runtime lowering, explicit agent activation, authentication and network exposure are separate choices.

A native C consumer or binding author must not read ABI presence as package parity, and must read what CI actually exercised before treating the C API workflows and release-gate inventory as executed evidence.
tokens: no workflow builds the C library

concepts.text: Native platform evidence has distinct classes: mapping tests, private-host runs, translated runs (Wine) and physical-host observation.

The minimum route to a first program: select a renderer when configuring, build CNA, derive from Game, let GraphicsDeviceManager create the device, load through ContentManager and draw with SpriteBatch.
Portable code stays within the Microsoft::Xna::Framework surface and treats CNAEXT-marked APIs as explicit extensions, which strict mode can check mechanically.

When a result differs by renderer, identify the public selector, implementation family, native or translation API and whether the intended route engaged, then reduce the case to a state transition, readback or pixel oracle; a successful process exit alone cannot localise a renderer-specific failure.
